note: Used before nouns: 대형 마트, 대형 버스.

ex.en: I go to the big-box store on weekends.
We bought a new large TV.
We rented a large bus for the trip.

en: to guide, show the way, show around

ex.en: I'll show you the way to the hotel.
The staff showed us to our seats.
If you come to Seoul, I'll show you around.

note: Everyday speech often uses 머리 for 'head/brains'.

ex.en: Your brain gets tired when you don't sleep.
Exercise is good for brain health too.

ex.s: 공부를 너무 많이 해서 뇌가 멈췄어요.
ex.en: I studied so much my brain stopped working.

note: Follows a modifier: 올 듯해요. Like 것 같다, slightly more formal.

ex.en: It looks like it's going to rain today.
Minho seems really tired.

ex.s: 이 식당은 가격이 좀 비싼 듯해요.
ex.en: This restaurant seems a bit pricey.

ex.s: 어른 두 명, 아이 한 명이요.
ex.en: Two adults and one child, please.
You should use polite speech with elders.

ex.s: 우리 아들이 이제 다 어른이 됐어요.
ex.en: Our son is all grown up now.

note: 충격(을) 받다 = to be shocked.

ex.en: I was shocked when I heard the news.
The movie's ending was a real shock.
This case holds up well to impact.

note: ㅎ-irregular: 저래요, 저런, 저렇게.

ex.en: Why is that person acting like that?
I want a bag like that.
You shouldn't do it like that.

ex.s: 이 일은 경력이 몇 년 필요해요?
ex.en: How many years of experience does this job need?
I have five years of experience as a nurse.
Personality matters more than experience.

note: 통화하다 = to talk on the phone. 통화 중 = on a call/busy.

ex.en: Is now a good time to talk?
I talked on the phone with my mom for an hour.
I'm on a call right now, so I'll call you later.

en: on earth, what in the world
note: Adds frustration or surprise to a question.

ex.en: Where on earth were you?
What on earth is this?
Why on earth is it so expensive?
Did you get a haircut? You look really different.

ex.s: 서울은 십 년 동안 많이 달라졌어요.
ex.en: Seoul has changed a lot in ten years.

ex.s: 날씨에 따라 계획이 달라질 수 있어요.
ex.en: Plans may change depending on the weather.
Ji-woo has a good sense of fashion.
Fashion changes so fast these days.
I often read fashion magazines.
Shall we have a course meal for dinner?
This hiking trail is a bit tough.
Did you plan our route for today?
The teacher pointed out my pronunciation.
Thanks for pointing out my mistake.
My team leader points out every little thing.
What time does the train leave?
I just left home.
Shall we set off early tomorrow morning?
The air conditioner isn't working.
This app works without the internet too.
The elevator is working again.
Did you go vote yesterday?
Let's vote on the lunch menu.
I voted for my friend for class president.
It's so cold out that my ears hurt.
The puppy's ears are really big.
My ears hurt from listening to loud music.
Please close the door.

ex.s: 그 가게는 몇 시에 문 닫아요?
ex.en: What time does that store close?
It's cold, so I'll close the window.

note: Often 자동으로 = automatically.

ex.en: The door opens automatically.
My car is an automatic.
I pay rent by automatic transfer.

note: 부상을 당하다 = to get injured.

ex.en: I got injured playing soccer.
Luckily, the injury isn't serious.

ex.s: 그 선수는 부상 때문에 경기에 못 나와요.
ex.en: That player is out because of an injury.
The robot vacuum is really convenient.
My son loves robot toys.
At that restaurant, a robot brings the food.

note: Opposite: 끄다 (to turn off).

ex.en: Please turn on the light.
It was hot, so I turned on the AC.
I fell asleep with the TV on.

note: ㄹ drops before ㄴ/ㅂ/ㅅ: 는, 늡니다. Transitive: 늘리다.

ex.en: Your Korean has improved a lot.
I'm busy these days because work has increased.
The café has gotten a lot more customers.
I'll love you forever.
I'll remember this moment forever.
I can't wait forever.
This place is definitely tastier.
I don't know for sure what time they're coming.
It's definitely gotten colder.

en: to resemble, look like, take after
note: Usually past form for the state: 엄마를 닮았어요.

ex.en: The daughter looks a lot like her dad.

ex.s: 우리 둘이 닮았다는 말을 자주 들어요.
ex.en: People often tell us we look alike.
I take after my grandmother in personality.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 가벼워요, 가벼운.

ex.en: This bag is really light.
Shall we have a light lunch?
It's just a mild cold.

note: Only before nouns: 오랜 친구. Related: 오랜만이에요 = long time no see.

ex.en: I met an old friend yesterday.
I waited a long time.
A trip to Korea is my long-held dream.
Please answer the question honestly.
I couldn't answer the teacher's question.
The child answered loudly.
Kevin is our team leader.
A good leader listens well.
I was the leader for this trip.

note: Often after a time word: 일주일 내내, 여름 내내.

ex.en: I stayed home all weekend.
It rained all week.
I cried the whole time I watched the movie.

note: Mostly in compounds: 항공권 (plane ticket), 항공사 (airline).

ex.en: Did you book the plane tickets?
Which airline are you flying?
I sent the package by airmail.
What's your budget?
Our budget for this trip is a bit tight.
I chose a gift within my budget.

ex.s: 오늘 최저 기온이 영하 오 도예요.
ex.en: Today's low is minus five degrees.
This store has the lowest price.
The minimum hourly wage went up this year.
Extra cheese, please.
I added a friend on KakaoTalk.
I added a meeting to the schedule.
I'm not good at math.
I have a math test tomorrow.
My daughter wants help with her math homework.

en: to take (an exam); pay; hold (an event)
note: 으-irregular: 치러요, 치렀어요 (not 치뤘어요).

ex.en: I took the exam yesterday.
I paid for it in cash.
We had our wedding last week.

en: to be used; to be written

ex.en: This room is used for storage.
This word is used often.
It's written in English on the menu.
What symptoms do you have?
I have some cold symptoms.
If the symptoms continue, see a doctor.

note: 르-irregular: 잘라요, 잘랐어요.

ex.en: I cut my hair short.
Please cut the meat into small pieces.
I cut the paper with scissors.

en: to be a pity, sad, unfortunate
note: ㅂ-irregular: 안타까워요. 안타깝게도 = unfortunately.

ex.en: It's such a shame you didn't pass the test.
It was a good store; it's sad it closed.
Unfortunately, the tickets are sold out.
I'll look it up online.
I searched for good restaurants nearby.
Try looking up what that word means.
I listen to the radio when I drive.
This song came on the radio.
Please turn the radio down.
The bird hurt its wing.
The wings are the best part of the chicken.
My seat is by the airplane wing.
I left my luggage at the hotel.
Leave this to me.
On weekends I leave my dog with a friend.
How do I connect to the Wi-Fi?
I connected the speaker via Bluetooth.
I'll put you through to the person in charge.
I have way too many assignments today.
When is the assignment due?
I got a new task at work.

note: 전통적 = traditional (adjectival).

ex.en: We eat traditional food on Lunar New Year.
This market has a long tradition.
Our family values tradition.

note: 소개하다 = to introduce. 소개팅 = blind date.

ex.en: Please briefly introduce yourself.
I met my husband through a friend.

ex.s: 좋은 식당 소개 좀 해 주세요.
ex.en: Please recommend a good restaurant.

note: Homonym 용기 also means 'container'.

ex.en: I worked up the courage and said it.
Traveling alone takes courage.
Thanks for encouraging me.
I'm moving next month.
I moved near my office.
It rained on moving day.

note: More formal than 사다; common on signs and websites.

ex.en: Please buy your tickets online.
I bought a new laptop.
Where did you buy it?
My knees hurt when I climb stairs.
I fell and hurt my knee.
The child sat on her mom's lap.

note: 눈물이 나다 = to tear up.

ex.en: I teared up watching the movie.
Cutting onions makes me tear up.
I'm so happy I'm crying.
I signed up for a yoga class.
Where do I apply for a visa?
I applied for a new card.
The cat got scared and ran away.
Don't run away from your problems.
I saw a bug and ran off screaming.

note: Passive: 변경되다 (to be changed).

ex.en: I'd like to change my reservation date.
I changed my password.
Can I change the delivery address?
My computer got a virus.

ex.s: 손을 자주 씻으면 바이러스를 막을 수 있어요.
ex.en: Washing your hands often helps stop viruses.
Colds are caused by viruses.

en: to quit; to hang up; to cut off

ex.en: I quit smoking.
I'm trying to give up coffee.
I'm going to hang up now.
How do I get rid of this smell?
I deleted all the apps I don't use.
I exercise to get rid of stress.

note: Also a polite way to address an elderly man.

ex.en: My grandfather is eighty this year.
I'm going to my grandpa's house this weekend.
Please have a seat here, sir.

note: 연습하다 = to practice.

ex.en: I practice the piano every day.
I need more pronunciation practice.
What time is soccer practice today?

en: to be ruined, go under; to blow it
note: Casual 망했다 = 'I'm doomed' or 'I blew it.'

ex.s: 그 식당은 일 년 만에 망했어요.
ex.en: That restaurant went under after a year.
I bombed the test.
The rain ruined the picnic.

note: 관광하다 = to go sightseeing. 관광객 = tourist.

ex.en: Tomorrow we'll go sightseeing downtown.
This city is famous for tourism.
Where's the tourist information center?
Just hold still for a second.
The kid can't sit still.
Now that I think about it, I was wrong.

en: early morning, dawn; the wee hours
note: Roughly midnight to sunrise: 새벽 세 시 = 3 a.m.

ex.en: I woke up at 3 a.m.
I played games until the early morning.
The plane arrives in the early morning.
Do you know how to play the guitar?
Wei played the piano at the wedding.
Someone is playing the violin at the subway station.
Ready? Let's go!
Dinner's ready.
Your drink is ready.
Grandma loves tending her garden.
Lots of flowers bloomed in the garden.
I want to live in a house with a yard.
This game has simple rules.
I like simple designs.
My husband is pretty uncomplicated.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 아쉬워요. Mild regret, often when something good ends.

ex.en: You're leaving already? That's a shame.
It's a shame the vacation is over.
It was tasty, but the portion was a bit small.

note: 매력적이다 = attractive, charming.

ex.en: That person has charm.
This city's appeal is its food.
Sofía's charm is her honesty.

note: Two different words. 사과하다 = to apologize.

ex.en: How much is one apple?
I eat an apple every morning.
I'll apologize first.
Come a little closer.
My office is close to my home.
I waited nearly an hour.

note: 놀이터 = playground. 놀이공원 = amusement park.

ex.en: Kids learn through play.
We're going to an amusement park this weekend.
The kids are playing on the playground.

note: Eaten with rice. 국물 = broth. 찌개 is a thicker stew.

ex.s: 한국 사람은 밥이랑 국을 같이 먹어요.
ex.en: Koreans eat rice and soup together.
The soup is a bit salty.
We eat seaweed soup on birthdays.
Don't force yourself to eat.
I forced a smile for the photo.
I went to the work dinner against my will.

ex.s: 이 가게는 이익이 별로 안 나요.
ex.en: This store doesn't make much profit.
It's something that benefits both of us.

ex.s: 작은 이익 때문에 친구를 잃으면 안 돼요.
ex.en: Don't lose a friend over a small gain.

note: 신용카드 = credit card.

ex.en: I'll pay by credit card.
You need a good credit score to get a loan.
That person can't be trusted.

note: Opposite: 후반 (latter part).

ex.en: I'm in my early thirties.
The beginning of the movie was a bit boring.
Let's meet early next month.

note: Often number + 연속 (이틀 연속) or 연속으로.

ex.en: It's rained three days in a row.
I worked late two nights in a row.

ex.s: 우리 팀이 다섯 번 연속 이겼어요.
ex.en: Our team won five times in a row.

note: 요청하다 = to request.

ex.en: I sent you the documents you requested.
I sent you a friend request.
If you need help, just ask.

ex.s: 박물관 내부는 사진 촬영이 안 돼요.
ex.en: You can't take photos inside the museum.
The inside of the car is really clean.
That's an internal company matter.
I studied literature in college.
Can you recommend a book of Korean literature?
Literature class is the most fun.
Let's meet at the square.
There's a show in the square this weekend.
Have you been to Gwanghwamun Square?

note: 해석하다 = to interpret/translate (text). Spoken interpreting is 통역.

ex.s: 이 문장 해석 좀 해 주세요.
ex.en: Please translate this sentence for me.
Everyone interprets it differently.
Do you believe in dream interpretation?

note: Set phrases: 폐를 끼치다 (to impose), 영향을 끼치다 (to influence).

ex.en: Sorry to impose on you.
I'm sorry for the inconvenience.
My mom had a big influence on me.
It's illegal to park here.
Don't download things illegally.
There are lots of illegally parked cars on the street.

note: 절하다 = to bow deeply (e.g., to elders on 설날).

ex.en: This weekend I went to a temple in the mountains.
This temple is over a thousand years old.
I bowed to my grandma on Lunar New Year.
There's a coffee mark left on my clothes.
There are signs someone ate the cake.
Traces of our trip remain in the photos.
Don't worry about how others see you.
I can feel people looking at me.
That dress drew everyone's attention.
My friend is a researcher at a hospital.
The researchers are having a meeting.
My older sister works as a researcher.

note: For truly admirable people or deeds, not 'great' as in 'nice'.

ex.en: Moms are truly amazing.
King Sejong was a great king.
I saw a great musician perform.

note: 보고하다 = to report. 보고서 = written report.

ex.en: I reported to my team leader.
Please give me an update after the meeting.
I have to write a report by tomorrow.

note: 창문 is the more common word for a house window.

ex.en: May I open the window?
It's quiet now that the window's closed.
Try opening the link in a new window.
The server is down.
I can't connect to the game server.
I uploaded the file to the company server.
The voice actor in this cartoon has a nice voice.
As a kid, I dreamed of being a voice actor.
That voice actor is in commercials too.
What material does the test cover?
That's beyond my budget.
This is outside the delivery area.

note: Used before nouns: 공공장소 (public place), 공공 화장실.

ex.en: Please be quiet in public places.
Be careful when using public Wi-Fi.
Is there a public restroom around here?
